title: Orchestral fallback coordination for matrixed rollouts
text:
Orchestral fallback coordination for matrixed rollouts

description:
Problem statement: During a recent staged rollout of model-omega across Hosted, Dedicated and Private planes we observed correlated quality regressions in canary slices that manifested differently per topology: Hosted showed elevated token-level hallucination rates, Dedicated tenants saw increased tail latency under batching, and Private deployments surfaced sticky KV-cache divergence. Existing rollback playbooks handle single-plane rollbacks but do not coordinate simultaneous, tenant-aware fallbacks across heterogeneous deployments. This ticket defines an orchestral fallback flow: a coordinated, observable, and reversible procedure for cross-plane regressions that minimizes scope of impact and communicates clearly to customers.

acceptance_criteria:
A reusable runbook exists that operators can execute to simultaneously quiesce new variants in Hosted, Dedicated and Private without causing KV cache corruption or double-processing.
Automated orchestration script (ops/fallback-orchestrator) can trigger safe variant pinning + kvcache invalidation for a specified tenant slice within 3 minutes end-to-end in staging.
Customer communication templates (support & field) prepared and validated for high-impact regressions, with one-click insertion of per-tenant mitigation state.
Post-mortem checklist items (metrics to collect, required traces, and evaluation prompt set) are parameterized and produced automatically after a coordinated fallback.
Runbook tested in a canary rehearsal with the oncall rotation and documented in Confluence with links to the test dashboard.

steps:
1) Triage: confirm regression signature (quality, latency, or cache) and affected tenant list via rollout-slice filter in the Console.
2) Scope: build a 'tenant matrix' (tenant IDs x deployment planes) to identify where to apply variant pin or fallback.
3) Quiesce traffic: apply soft traffic-slice hold for targeted tenants using routing policy 'slice-hold' to avoid state divergence.
4) KV handling: run kvcache-export for affected hosts, then perform a coordinated KV drain + invalidate on the new variant only, followed by safe cache warmup on the pinned variant.
5) Model pin: roll traffic to pinned variant with canary-weight=0 for new variant, confirm SLOs then lift slice-hold.
6) Communication: publish templated customer notification and update the Incident in the support tracker with mitigation state and ETA.
7) Postmortem: collect traces, per-token diffs, evaluation prompt set, and schedule regression rendezvous with Applied ML.

2025-02-20 09:14 - Aisha Raman: Created ticket after post-shift incident review. Attached initial notes and symptom timeline. Requesting ops + runtime + applied-ml reps for scoping.
2025-02-21 11:02 - Diego Cortez: Spike complete in staging. Prototype orchestrator can pin variants across hosted and dedicated but we observed KV staleness when Private plane is involved due to differing cache topology. Filing follow-up to add per-plane cache adapters.
2025-02-22 15:50 - Mei Tan (Applied ML): Observed that hallucination regressions align with a tokenization edge-case introduced in model-omega. Short-term mitigation: pin previous tokenizer variant in Hosted and Private; long-term: push tokenization fix. Need model-team signoff.
2025-02-24 08:33 - Diego Cortez: Drafted customer notification templates and added them to Confluence. PR for ops scripts opened (ops-scripts #274). Requesting oncall rehearsal on 2025-03-03.
2025-03-03 10:12 - Oncall (rotation-6): Rehearsal executed in staging with synthetic tenant slices. Observed orchestrator latency ~110s for a 10-tenant matrix (target <180s). KV invalidation step required an additional compensating warmup step; updated runbook step 4. Noted: add guard against cross-plane kvcache-ttl mismatch.
2025-03-03 12:45 - Priya Shah (Support): Approved customer comms templates. Suggested adding 'short-term workaround' checkbox for partners on Dedicated contracts. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-03 14:20 - Diego Cortez: Next actions: finalize PRs, add per-plane adapters (ops-scripts #276), schedule a dry-run with a real tenant (consent required) during maintenance window. Assigned follow-up ENG-128901 for partner-specific fallback flows.
